title: Write an evidence-safe incident update
summary: Select changing incident signals and write a concise update for the next owner without overstating the cause.
learningObjectives: Select relevant incident facts from monitoring, team messages and ownership notes.
Separate observed impact from an unconfirmed cause.
Write an actionable handoff update with owner, next step and request.

sections.title: Use the F-I-A-R workflow
sections.body:
FACT — What is directly observed?
IMPACT — Who or what is affected, and how much?
ACTION — What is happening next, and who owns it?
REQUEST — What decision or help is needed, and by when?

Keep a suspected cause explicitly uncertain until evidence confirms it.

expressions.meaning: Nêu fact có timestamp và phân biệt giá trị ban đầu với giá trị mới.
expressions.example: At 22:08, the checkout 503 rate rose from 0.7% to 31%.

expressions.meaning: Nối technical signal với impact hữu ích cho audience.
expressions.example: This is affecting checkout by reducing the success rate to 68%.

expressions.phrase: We are checking whether ___; this is not confirmed.
expressions.meaning: Nêu hypothesis nhưng giữ ranh giới bằng chứng.
expressions.example: We are checking whether the timeout change exhausted the pool; this is not confirmed.
alternatives: The strongest lead is ___, but the cause is not confirmed.

expressions.meaning: Nêu owner cùng action đang diễn ra.
expressions.example: Lan owns diagnosis and is currently comparing pool metrics with the release diff.

expressions.meaning: Đưa ra một request có owner, decision và deadline.
expressions.example: Platform lead, please decide by 22:30 whether to assign rollback access.

sections.title: Worked signal map from a notification incident
sections.content:
Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Observed fact: push delivery fell to 72% at 14:06 after release 5.8.
Impact: password-reset notifications may arrive late.
Hypothesis: the new batch size may be exhausting worker memory; this is not confirmed.
Action/owner: Jo is comparing worker memory before and after 5.8.
Request: Release lead, decide by 14:25 whether to pause the rollout.
Noise to omit: the dashboard theme changed this morning.

exercises.question: Which sentence keeps fact and hypothesis separate?
options: Push delivery fell to 72% after release 5.8; Jo is checking whether the new batch size increased memory use.
correctAnswer: Push delivery fell to 72% after release 5.8; Jo is checking whether the new batch size increased memory use.
exercises.explanation: The timing and delivery rate are observed; the memory explanation remains a hypothesis being checked.

exercises.question: Which request gives the audience a decision and deadline?
options: Release lead, please decide by 14:25 whether to pause the rollout while Jo compares memory.
correctAnswer: Release lead, please decide by 14:25 whether to pause the rollout while Jo compares memory.
exercises.explanation: It names the decision owner, requested decision and useful deadline.

exercises.question: Which sentence reports the relevant impact without adding an unsupported cause?
options: Push delivery is at 72%, so password-reset notifications may arrive late.
Push delivery fell after release 5.8, so the new batch size caused delayed password resets.
Push delivery is at 72%; the team is investigating, but customer impact is not yet known.
correctAnswer: Push delivery is at 72%, so password-reset notifications may arrive late.
exercises.explanation: It connects the observed delivery rate to the supplied customer impact without turning the batch-size hypothesis into a cause or hiding known impact.

performanceTask.title: Post the incident handoff update
performanceTask.scenario: You are the communication lead for a distributed engineering incident.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Cold attempt: use only the job evidence above. Write the update you would post now. Do not invent a confirmed root cause.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Write a 70–110 word update in English using F-I-A-R. Keep observed facts separate from the connection-pool hypothesis, name the current owner and ask the platform lead for one decision before handover.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Checkout 503s rose to 31% of attempts at 22:08, six minutes after release 2.4 began. The pool warning is the strongest lead, but it does not confirm the root cause; Lan is comparing pool metrics with the release diff. Lan owns diagnosis, while rollback access remains unassigned. Platform lead, could you name the rollback owner by 22:30, before the 22:35 handover? I propose that support ask affected customers to retry once while the team monitors the error rate; four of six reported customers succeeded after one retry.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Rewrite your update using the selected retry focus. Keep every fact traceable to an artifact and preserve any uncertainty that is not resolved.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Unseen transfer: write a 70–110 word update for the storage on-call using only this new evidence. Include observed impact, one cautious hypothesis, current action/owner and one decision request.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Delayed retrieval: write a fresh 70–110 word update for the messaging handover. Do not look for or reconstruct your earlier checkout response.

rubric.label: Fact and hypothesis
rubric.description: Every fact is traceable to an artifact and any unconfirmed cause is framed as a hypothesis.

rubric.label: Audience-relevant impact
rubric.description: Quantifies the useful impact and omits unrelated noise.

rubric.label: Owner, action and request
rubric.description: Names the current owner/next step and asks the audience for one decision by a useful deadline.
